findings_addressed.oracle: Two independent oracles: (1) _get_windows_gpu_info() + _check_intel_driver() derive oracle_driver_ok and the canonical driver-missing warning string without going through check_windows_requirements(); (2) sys.getwindowsversion() derives whether the Windows-version component can set met=False. From these two sources the test derives expected_met = oracle_version_met AND oracle_driver_ok and asserts met == expected_met unconditionally.
findings_addressed.documented_mutation: In src/intellicrack/providers/xpu_utils.py line 631: change `if not driver_ok:` to `if True:` — the driver-missing warning is then appended unconditionally even when an Intel Arc GPU with a driver IS present (oracle_driver_ok=True), breaking `assert driver_missing_warning not in warnings` on a machine where the Intel Arc driver IS installed (e.g. Intel Arc B580).
findings_addressed.anti_pattern_eliminated: N6 (if-result-guarded vacuous assertion) — the previous test guarded its only load-bearing assertions inside `if not oracle_driver_ok:`, which is never entered on the target machine (Intel Arc B580, driver present). The replacement test uses unconditional assertions that cover both the driver-present and driver-absent branches, with expected_met derived from independent oracles.

notes: The previous test was non-falsifiable on the target machine (Windows + Intel Arc B580) because oracle_driver_ok=True, so the `if not oracle_driver_ok:` guard never executed. The rehardened test adds unconditional assertions: (1) met==expected_met where expected_met is derived from sys.getwindowsversion() AND oracle_driver_ok independently; (2) when oracle_driver_ok=True, the canonical driver-missing warning string must NOT be in warnings — falsifiable by mutating the production if-not-driver_ok branch to if True. Both assertions execute on the normal driver-present path.
